cards.text: New king in Judah, friend. Ahaz son of Jotham takes the throne at twenty years old and reigns in Jerusalem sixteen years, while Pekah son of Remaliah, king of Israel, is in his seventeenth year. And unlike David his father, Ahaz does not do what was right in the eyes of the LORD his God.

cards.question: King Ahaz turns away from what's right in the eyes of the LORD. Whose ways does he walk in instead?

cards.text: And then it gets darker. Ahaz even sacrifices his son in the fire, following the abominations of the nations the LORD had driven out before the Israelites.

cards.question: King Ahaz is following the ways of the nations the LORD drove out. Where does he sacrifice and burn incense?

answers.text: On the high places and under every green tree
Only at the temple in Jerusalem
Only in the courts of his palace

cards.text: Under EVERY green tree, friend, and that is a whole lot of trees. Then Rezin, king of Aram, and Pekah, king of Israel, come up to wage war against Jerusalem, but their siege can't overcome Ahaz.
But at that time Rezin recovers Elath for Aram and drives out the men of Judah. He sends the Edomites into Elath, and they live there to this day.

cards.question: Jerusalem holds, but Judah just lost Elath to Aram. Who does King Ahaz send messengers to for help?

cards.text: So Ahaz sends messengers to Tiglath-pileser, king of Assyria. Two kings came against his walls, and Ahaz scrolls straight to the BIGGEST name in his contacts.

cards.question: What does King Ahaz ask Tiglath-pileser, king of Assyria, to do?

answers.text: Save him from the kings of Aram and Israel
Win back the town of Elath for Judah
Make peace between Judah and Edom

cards.question: King Ahaz wants the king of Assyria to save him. In his message, what does Ahaz call himself?

cards.text: Servant AND son? Friend, that's not a letter, that's adoption paperwork. And Ahaz doesn't send it empty-handed.

cards.question: Ahaz sends a gift to the king of Assyria along with his message. What is it?

answers.text: Silver and gold from the LORD's house and the palace
Horses and chariots from the royal stables
Bronze and iron from the city armories

cards.text: The king of Assyria responds to him and marches up to Damascus. Put some silver and gold in the mix, friend, and suddenly the king of Assyria is ALL ears.

cards.question: The king of Assyria captures Damascus and puts Rezin to death.
The king of Assyria takes the people of Damascus to ___ as captives.

cards.text: With Damascus captured, King Ahaz goes there to meet Tiglath-pileser, king of Assyria. And while he's in Damascus, he sees the altar there.
Ahaz sends Uriah the priest a model of the altar and complete plans for building it. That's somebody on vacation texting their contractor a photo and the measurements before they've even unpacked.

cards.question: King Ahaz sends Uriah the priest a model of the Damascus altar and complete plans for it. What does Uriah do?

answers.text: Builds the altar by Ahaz's instructions
Sends the plans back to Damascus
Locks the plans away in the temple

cards.question: Uriah the priest finishes building the altar before King Ahaz gets back from Damascus.
When King Ahaz comes back from Damascus and sees the new altar, he approaches it and presents offerings on it.

cards.text: He offers his burnt offering and his grain offering, pours out his drink offering and splatters the blood of his peace offerings on the new altar. Friend, that's not a test run. That's a GRAND OPENING with the ribbon AND the big scissors.
So now there are TWO altars out front. The new one, and the bronze altar that stood before the LORD, sitting between the new altar and the house of the LORD.

cards.question: What does King Ahaz do with the bronze altar that stood before the LORD?

answers.text: Moves it to the north side of the new altar
Sends it off to the king of Assyria
Breaks it apart and melts down the bronze

cards.text: Then King Ahaz gives Uriah the priest his orders. He says he'll use the bronze altar himself, to seek guidance.

cards.question: King Ahaz keeps the bronze altar for seeking guidance. So which altar gets the morning burnt offering, the evening grain offering and all the people's offerings?

answers.text: The altars on the high places

cards.text: Friend, that new altar just got put on EVERY shift, morning AND evening, no lunch break. And all the blood of the burnt offerings and sacrifices gets splattered on it too.

cards.question: Uriah the priest pushes back on King Ahaz's commands about the altars.

cards.text: Ahaz cuts off the frames of the movable stands, removes the bronze basin from each one and takes down the Sea from the bronze oxen that were under it. This man is pulling things off and moving things around like he's got his own home makeover show.

cards.question: King Ahaz takes the Sea down off the bronze oxen and puts it on a ___ base.

cards.text: Then he removes the Sabbath canopy they had built in the temple and closes the royal entryway outside the house of the LORD. The KING'S entryway, and the king closes it. I'm not making this up, friend.

cards.question: Why does King Ahaz remove the Sabbath canopy and close the royal entryway?

answers.text: On account of the king of Assyria
On account of the new altar
On account of Uriah the priest

cards.text: The rest of Ahaz's acts are written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah, so if you want the extended cut, that's where it lives. Then Ahaz rests with his fathers and is buried with them in the City of David.

cards.question: After Ahaz is buried in the City of David, which son of his reigns in his place?
